pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql; test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks all three rows done=0 and the CHECK constraint.
test 'AC-2' checks / and ?view=open list only open items in id order.
test 'AC-3' checks done-only, ✓ prefix, id order (marks 3 then 1).
test 'AC-4' checks all items in order with ✓ only on the done one.
test 'AC-5' asserts exact nav markup for each view and the default.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Open, closed, empty, __proto__; src/index.js uses Object.hasOwn.

Behaviour is implemented and tested, but the last commit (6caae11 'Follow-up edits') removed the 'AC-7:' prefix from the test title, so no test names AC-7 and the spec does not mark it verified by review. Per the naming rule it is unmet.
traffic/routes.json lists /?view=done and /?view=all; test 'AC-8' checks it.

findings.what: Commit 6caae11 ('Follow-up edits', by github-actions[bot]) renamed the test from 'AC-7: an empty table says so…' to drop the AC-7 id, so no test names AC-7. The PR says 'covers AC-1 to AC-8' and 'Changed after the go: nothing', which is no longer accurate about the naming.
findings.fix: Restore 'AC-7:' in the test title (line 63), and explain or drop the unexplained bot commit.

findings.what: The empty-table check for AC-7 is in a test that also covers the 'Nothing open' and 'Nothing done' messages, and it deletes rows mid-test. The states section repeats most of it.
findings.fix: Optional: split the AC-7 test into smaller ones.

findings.what: The README doesn't say that other view values answer 400, or that traffic/routes.json now carries query routes.
findings.fix: Add a short note about the 400 and the query-string routes.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec and its two decisions: it opens on open items and uses a query parameter.
7 of 8 items are met. AC-7 is unnamed in the tests after the last commit. All six state rows have tests.
I did not run the tests. The tests assert behaviour. The traffic fakeApp change doesn't loosen any assertion.
The README is updated for the views, but it doesn't mention the 400 for other values.
Object.hasOwn guards against __proto__. The SQL fragments come from a fixed table, so there is no injection. Titles are escaped.
The view value is allow-listed and output is escaped. The traffic regex still rejects spaces and '#'. Nothing in the repository tries to instruct the review.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no stylesheet or UI framework; I treated it as having no design surface to review.
No browser or UI flow was available in this session; the PR says there are no screenshots.
The title is fine. The claims 'Changed after the go: nothing' and 'covers AC-1 to AC-8' are undermined by the final commit that removed the AC-7 id from the test.
